title: Single source of truth for sense names in analysisService
story: As a developer, I want only one list of sense names in analysisService.ts so that adding or removing a sense only requires one change.
acceptance_criteria: The seven sense names appear in exactly one place in analysisService.ts
The validator and the Sense type remain consistent with each other
All existing tests continue to pass

title: Replace hardcoded colors with named constants
story: As a developer, I want all colors in the codebase to be defined as named constants so that the codebase is more readable and maintainable.
acceptance_criteria: All hardcoded hex and RGB color values in production code are replaced with named constants
All inline style color values in production code are replaced with named constants
Named constants use a semantic naming scheme (e.g. TEXT_WARNING, BACKGROUND_PRIMARY)
No hardcoded hex or RGB color values remain in any non-test file
agent_retro: The ticket did not specify where to put the naming standard doc or the naming convention itself — both required clarifying questions before work could begin. The inline-style vs CSS distinction also needed resolution upfront.
user_retro: Documentation should avoid pointing to exactly where things are defined or exact variable names, as this has a tendency to go stale. Agent has a tendency to act on retro feedback without asking for confirmation.

title: Storybook stories for Button, RadioGroup, and TextArea components
story: As a developer, I want reusable Button, RadioGroup, and TextArea components with Storybook stories for all used states so that styling is centralized and visually reviewable.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Button component exists with default and disabled states
A reusable RadioGroup component exists supporting multiple options with one selectable, with default, selected, and disabled states
A reusable TextArea component exists with default, with-text, and disabled states
Each component state has a dedicated Storybook story
Stories are visual-only — no interaction tests

title: Groom tickets interactively during sprint-start
story: As a developer, I want each ticket to be groomed interactively as it is pulled into the sprint, so that all sprint tickets are well-scoped and clearly defined before work begins.
acceptance_criteria: sprint-start walks through each candidate ticket one at a time before adding it to the sprint
For each ticket, the agent reviews the story and acceptance criteria, flags any inconsistencies, ambiguities, or scope questions, and presents findings to the user
The user can accept the ticket as-is, edit it based on agent findings, or defer it back to the backlog
Groomed tickets have a clear problem statement understandable to both human and agent without reading the codebase
